keyECGEvidence: Pre-event note indicates baseline conduction issues (LBBB-like)
modelResponse.mechanism: The VT is likely a manifestation of myocardial irritability secondary to chronic ischemic heart disease and underlying cardiomyopathy, exacerbated by volume overload.

rejectedAlternatives.why: The presence of AV dissociation and wide, sustained QRS morphology strongly favors VT over aberrantly conducted atrial tachycardia.
Potassium is within reference range (4.3 mmol/L), and Magnesium is adequate (2.1 mg/dL).
No digoxin level is provided in the data.

recommendedActions: STAT activation of Rapid Response Team/Code Team due to hypotension (SBP 88 mmHg) and VT.
Initiate synchronized cardioversion if patient remains unstable or if VT is sustained and hemodynamically compromised.
Administer IV fluids cautiously to support BP, monitoring response closely given cardiac status.
Hold all antiarrhythmic medications if VT is refractory or if hypotension persists, per cardiology protocol.
Review diuretic regimen in light of renal function and volume status; consider titration of vasodilators if tolerated.
uncertainty: The exact trigger for the VT (ischemic vs. structural remodeling) cannot be definitively separated with the provided data alone.
